title: Building safe Payment Infrastructure for the autonomous economy — Steve Kaliski, Stripe
talk_summary: Stripe's Steve Kaliski describes payment primitives for AI agents: shared payment tokens that scope a credential to a seller, amount, currency and time window; a 402-based machine payments protocol for paid tool calls; and an agent-to-commerce checkout protocol that returns structured cart state instead of scraping UIs. The core thesis is to keep discovery non-deterministic but make credentials, payments and checkout strictly deterministic and API-driven.

takeaways.technique: Scoped capability tokens instead of raw credentials
takeaways.what_they_do: The agent provisions a token that is enforced server-side to a specific seller, amount, currency and expiry, so even a mis-parsed price or spoofed domain cannot cause overspend; the seller still receives brand/last-four for its own risk checks.
takeaways.evidence_quote: this Visa card, which has a much higher credit limit, is only going to work for $25 and it's only going to work for the next 30 days
takeaways.numbers: $25 limit, 30-day expiry; $50 request rejected, lowered amount passed

takeaways.technique: Machine-readable 402 challenge for paid tool calls
takeaways.what_they_do: Protected HTTP endpoints return a 402 with an encoded payload describing what is being bought, from whom, and how to pay; the agent pays and retries, getting structured success plus a transaction record.
takeaways.evidence_quote: communicate the need to pay um in those HP requests by returning a 402 status code, and then supply that credential

takeaways.technique: Deterministic transaction layer under a non-deterministic planner
takeaways.what_they_do: Explicitly separates the LLM's exploratory/planning role from the execution of irreversible actions, which are done through structured APIs with verifiable parties and enforced constraints.
takeaways.evidence_quote: discovery and exploration benefit from non-determinism ... But credentials, payments, and checkout require determinism

takeaways.technique: Structured state relay instead of UI scraping
takeaways.what_they_do: Sellers expose product catalog and cart state as JSON and relay updated state on every agent action (quantity, shipping, payment method), so the agent never has to parse a rendered page.
takeaways.evidence_quote: instead of the robot trying to, you know, pull information, you know, out of a UI like this, it has structured data that I can refer to

takeaways.technique: Recurring scoped mandates for periodic spend
takeaways.what_they_do: A credential can carry a periodic budget (e.g. $25/week) and request subsequent usage like an OAuth refresh flow, rather than re-issuing unlimited credentials.
takeaways.evidence_quote: you can sort of like request uh subsequent usage
